title: Clean-up Effort, Assessment of Impact and Review of Safeguards following Oil Spill from Accident at Pasir Panjang Terminal
what_it_is: Clean-up Effort, Assessment of Impact and Review of Safeguards following Oil Spill from Accident at Pasir Panjang Terminal

sections.label: Pasir Panjang oil spill costs
sections.summary: Questions ask whether an environmental damage assessment was done and who bears clean-up costs after the 14 June 2024 Pasir Panjang Terminal accident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether any environmental damage assessment has been done in relation to the maritime accident at Pasir Panjang Terminal on 14 June 2024; (b) what is the estimated cost of clean-up operations thus far; and (c) who will bear the cost of the clean-up operations.

sections.label: Oil spill cost estimates
sections.summary: Question asks for estimated environmental costs, economic costs and clean-up costs from the Pasir Panjang Terminal oil spill, including emergency cleaning services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport with regard to the recent oil spill incident at Pasir Panjang Terminal, what are the estimated (i) environmental costs (ii) economic costs and (iii) costs of clean-up, including those arising from the procurement of emergency cleaning services.

sections.label: Beach and port clean-up costs
sections.summary: Question asks the estimated clean-up cost for beaches, coastal areas, port and territorial waters, including vessels, equipment and manpower for mitigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport in respect of the pollution caused by the oil spill at the Pasir Panjang Terminal on 14 June 2024, what is the estimated cost of the clean-up likely to be incurred for our beaches, coastal areas and port and territorial waters including the cost of deployment of vessels, equipment and manpower for all clean-up, containment and other mitigation measures.

sections.label: Boom deployment and worker safety
sections.summary: Questions ask about boom deployment timing, formation, length, freeboard, wave height, currents and breaks in the Vox Maxima and Marine Honour allision, and clean-up workers' safety equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport regarding the allision between Vox Maxima and Marine Honour (a) what time were booms fully deployed to encircle the vessels; (b) what was the boom formation shape and deployment pattern used; (c) what was the (i) total length of booms deployed (ii) height of the booms’ freeboard and skirt (iii) the significant wave height and (iv) the speed of tidal currents at the time and location of the incident; and (d) whether there were any breaks in the boom deployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment whether the workers involved in the clean-up efforts for the recent oil spill at Pasir Panjang Terminal have adequate personal safety protection equipment.

sections.label: Fish farms and water supply
sections.summary: Questions ask about food safety checks for fish farms, support for fish farm businesses, fish supply impact, and oil contamination testing at Jurong Island Desalination Plant.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in view of the recent oil spill at Pasir Panjang Terminal (a) whether the Singapore Food Agency will be conducting random checks on the quality of produce from the fish farms for a defined period to ensure food safety; (b) what other support can be offered to the fish farm businesses in addition to the booms that have been deployed; and (c) whether the local fish supply will be impacted in the short term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: asked asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) how frequently will the seawater intake at Jurong Island Desalination Plant be tested for oil contamination; and (b) whether there will be an impact on Singapore's water supply in the event that oil is detected.

sections.label: Marine park biodiversity impact
sections.summary: Questions ask the expected biodiversity impact of the oil spill on Sisters' Islands Marine Park and whether it affects plans for a second marine park.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what is the expected biodiversity impact of the recent Pasir Panjang Terminal oil spill on the Sisters' Islands Marine Park; (b) whether the impact of the oil spill will affect plans for the second marine park in the Southern Islands; and (c) if so, what is the anticipated impact.
